title: Floral Net Pattern Mehndi Design for Arm (No. 164)
descriptionParagraphs: Floral style, arm placement. You'll see butterfly wing and sunburst in it. We'd call it medium to draw, and a nice pick for Karva Chauth.

Henna on the forearm stains lighter than on the palm because the skin is thinner. Arm designs are easier to apply on someone else than on yourself, especially past the wrist. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.

Flowers are among the most common motifs in every henna tradition, from Indian and Pakistani mehndi to Arabic and Gulf styles. The lotus is a frequent motif in South Asian designs, where it is associated with purity and beauty.

Application tips: Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours. The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises.

image.alt: Floral Net Pattern mehndi design for arm henna pattern

faq.q: How can I make my mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.

faq.q: Should I do a patch test before applying mehndi?
faq.a: Yes. Apply a small amount of the paste to the inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if you have sensitive skin or are using a new cone.

faq.q: Which flowers are used most in mehndi designs?
faq.a: Roses, lotuses and simple five-petal flowers are the most common, usually joined by vines and leaves.

title: Floral Diamond Lattice Mehndi Design for Full Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A floral pattern for the full hand, built from petal arrangement and feather stroke. Difficulty: medium. Good for a wedding.

Full-hand designs run from the fingertips to the wrist, so allow extra time for application. Work from the wrist towards the fingers, or the other way round, so you never rest on wet paste. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.
Large roses with shaded petals are a signature of Arabic and Gulf-style henna. Vines and leaves are used to connect separate flowers into one flowing design.
Application tips: Wash and dry the skin before application and skip lotion or oil, which block the dye. Keeping the skin warm while the paste is on helps the colour develop.

title: Floral Diamond Lattice Mehndi Design for Back Hand
